selection: Held-out retrieval set authored blind to the discovery engine by four independent readers (derivation family, historical corpus-import, notes/literature, and exact/negative controls), each of whom read source passages with file reading and grep only and never ran workhouse discover, search, ask or why. No expected file or query of tests/fixtures/discovery_queries.json is reused. Every positive query paraphrases the mathematics of its target passage in different terminology (no file name, section label, DERIV/RESULT id or coined identifier from the passage; terminology_note records the wording avoided). A fifth validator pass checked mechanically that every expected path exists at the source commit, every text_any marker occurs in every expected file, source_review.lines lie inside the file, no query contains an expected file's basename stem or an expected id (outside the exact-control group), and no run of four or more consecutive words of a query appears verbatim in an expected file; eight queries were reworded and six marker lists repaired to pass, one thin companion file was dropped, and the negative-control greps were re-run over theory, docs, corpus-import, notes, paper, research, literature, ledger and src. It is a small purposive set, not a random sample or a mathematical validity benchmark.
relevance: A listed expected id, or a listed expected path with at least one text_any marker when markers are supplied. Historical sources remain relevant as dated records; retrieval does not endorse their current scientific status. Queries with negative true expect no relevant result and are reported as empty-result checks, excluded from positive-query recall and MRR.

queries.terminology_note: Near-miss: the corpus proves the simple-cubic plaquette graph is 12-regular and uses 'cubic' and 'hypercubic' throughout, but the body-centered cubic lattice never appears.

queries.query: Strong-coupling string tension for lattice gauge theory with the exceptional Lie group G_2 as gauge group

source_review.reason: grep -rIlE '\bG_2\b' theory docs corpus-import notes paper -> 0 text files; grep -rIlE 'exceptional (Lie|gauge|group)' -> 0; grep -rlE 'G\(2\)' (case-sensitive) -> 1 file, a Combes-Thomas extract where G(2) is a function value; case-sensitive '\bG2\b' hits (docs/referee/final_paper_2026-08-28.md, docs/validation/*.yaml, theory/superseded/MASTER_THEORY.md) are all the repository gap id G2 'Regenerate all displayed tables in canonical u'; the gauge groups the corpus treats are SU(N), with Sp(2N) and SO(N) appearing only in imported literature titles. Validator re-grep over research, literature, ledger and src as well: the only extra hit is one literature-manifest abstract (Diez-Miaskiwskyi Weingarten moments on general compact Lie groups) listing G_2 among worked examples; it is not a lattice string-tension source.

queries.terminology_note: Near-miss: 'string tension', 'strong coupling' and 'gauge group' are core corpus vocabulary for SU(N) (with literature mentions of Sp(2N) and SO(N)), but the exceptional group G_2 is never treated; the token G2 in the repository is the gap id G2 (table regeneration), not a group.
